_policy: Official sources only: .gov domains, the California Legislative Information service, the San Francisco Rent Board, and the U.S. Census Bureau API. Third-party legal blogs, property-management vendors and news aggregators were consulted to LOCATE official documents but are never cited as authority and no value was taken from them.

sources.title: Annual Rent Increase for 3/1/26 - 2/28/27 Announced
sources.publisher: City & County of San Francisco — Rent Board
sources.verifies: 1.6% allowable increase for 3/1/2026-2/28/2027; 1.4% for 3/1/2025-2/28/2026; worked calculation example

sources.title: 571 Allowable Annual Increases 26-27 (Info Sheet 571)
sources.verifies: The complete historical table of allowable annual increases from 4/1/1982 through 2/28/2027, including the 1992-93 single-increase caution

sources.title: Learn about rent increases in San Francisco
sources.verifies: 60%-of-CPI basis; once every 12 months; anniversary date mechanics; four worked examples; banked-increase forfeiture on a changed anniversary date; notice periods; base-rent-only rule; no rounding up; additional-occupant prohibition; vacancy decontrol

sources.title: Banked rent increases
sources.verifies: Banking mechanics; no limit; does not expire; new owners inherit; does not carry to a new tenant; notice content including which portion is banked; rent increase license cross-reference; CONTAINS the conflicting 24-month statement (Flag F-03)

sources.title: Annual rent increase for multiple years
sources.verifies: Adding up multi-year increases; no compounding; no petition needed; no rounding up; 30/35-day notice; base rent excludes passthroughs but includes parking and storage

sources.title: Current Rates, including Rent Increase, Relocation, Sec. Deposit
sources.verifies: 1.6% allowable increase; 4.2% security deposit interest; bankable Rent Board fee rows; capital improvement imputed interest rates; uncompensated labor rates; relocation payment amounts

sources.title: Learn about San Francisco rental laws
sources.verifies: June 13, 1979 coverage cutoff; Property Information Map as the verification tool; just cause overview; categories of units with eviction protection only; list of fully exempt unit types; Rent Board counselor contact

sources.title: Rent Board Rules and Regulations Part IV — Rent Increases Not Requiring Approval
sources.verifies: Rules § 4.10 (notice content; non-conforming increase null and void) and § 4.12 (banking; 12-month elapse requirement; no compounding; no rounding up; half-percent good-faith readjustment)

sources.title: The Rent Board Housing Inventory
sources.verifies: Rent increase license requirement; portal.sfrb.org; March 1 annual deadline; 7/1/2022 and 3/1/2023 phase-in; no monetary late penalty; license must be in effect on the effective date; submissions are public and under penalty of perjury; tenant lookup right

sources.title: Rent Board Rules § 13.14 Licensing — Notice of Rent Increase
sources.verifies: Unlicensed annual or banked increase is null and void; effective date (not service date) controls; banking rights survive a void increase

sources.title: Partial Exemption for Certain Single-Family Homes and Condominiums Under Costa-Hawkins
sources.verifies: A two-unit building is NOT exempt; single-family with legal or illegal in-law = two-unit building and not exempt; exemption still leaves just cause and Rent Board fee obligations; unabated-citation carve-out

sources.title: Charging for Additional Occupants Prohibited
sources.verifies: Increasing rent solely because an occupant was added is an unlawful rent increase even if the lease permits it; tenant petition can void it and recover overcharges; the only lawful route is an O&M or utility passthrough petition

sources.title: Rent Increases Under Section 6.14 And Costa-Hawkins
sources.verifies: Unlimited increase available only when the LAST ORIGINAL OCCUPANT vacates and a timely written 6.14 notice was served on each subsequent occupant (60 days generally reasonable); co-tenants are never subject to the Costa-Hawkins reset; no petition required but a tenant may petition to challenge

sources.title: Replacement of Roommates
sources.verifies: Tenant right to replace roommates; 14-day landlord response window; deemed approval on silence or unreasonable denial; Rules §§ 6.15A/6.15B/6.15D/6.15E grounds for denial; occupancy caps by bedroom count

sources.title: Algorithmic devices that set rent are prohibited in San Francisco
sources.verifies: Admin. Code § 37.10C effective 10/14/2024; definitions of algorithmic device and non-public competitor data; prohibitions on sale and use; per-month and per-unit violations; remedies up to $1,000 per violation plus fees; private right of action for tenants and tenants' rights organisations

sources.title: The California Tenant Protection Act of 2019 (AB 1482)
sources.verifies: 8.8% SF cap for 8/1/2026-7/31/2027 and the express statement that it does NOT apply to units under SF Rent Ordinance limitations; full exemption list including the two-unit owner-occupied exemption and the local-ordinance-more-restrictive exemption; Form 525 Report of Excessive Rent Increase

sources.title: Rent Board Forms Center
sources.verifies: Tenant petition forms 516A (decrease in housing services), 516B (failure to repair and maintain — available where a rent increase notice was received within the last 60 days), 516C (unlawful rent increase / rent history review), 516D (passthrough challenge), 517 (subtenant), 518 (tenant summary petition for a pending increase unlawful on its face)

sources.title: Index of Landlord and Tenant Information
sources.verifies: Authoritative list and numbering of Rent Board information topics used to locate S-03 through S-17

sources.title: Speak with a Rent Board counselor
sources.verifies: Free counseling; 415-252-4600; weekday hours; in-person at 25 Van Ness Ave Suite #700; multilingual support; counselors cannot give legal advice

sources.title: Tenant and Landlord Resources
sources.publisher: SF Mayor's Office of Housing and Community Development
sources.verifies: Free tenant legal help and counseling providers: Eviction Defense Collaborative, Bar Association of San Francisco Conflict Intervention Service, Housing Rights Committee, Bill Sorro Housing Program, Chinatown CDC, Mission Action, SOMCAN, Bayview-Hunters Point Tenants' Rights Clinic, Bay Area Legal Aid Consumer Rights Clinic; landlord-side resources: San Francisco Apartment Association, Rent Board

sources.title: California Civil Code § 827
sources.verifies: 30-day notice at 10% or less; 90-day notice above 10%; measurement against the lowest rent charged in the prior 12 months including combined increases; personal delivery or mail service under CCP § 1013

sources.title: California Civil Code § 1947.12 (AB 1482 rent cap)
sources.verifies: 5% + cost of living or 10% whichever is lower; two increments per 12 months; new-tenancy initial rent unrestricted; the § 1947.12(d)(3) local-rent-control exemption; the § 1947.12(d)(5) single-family/condo exemption and its REIT/corporation/LLC-with-corporate-member disqualification and written-notice condition

sources.title: California Civil Code § 1942.5 (retaliation)
sources.verifies: 180-day bar on increasing rent or decreasing services after specified tenant complaints; separate bar for retaliation against tenant organising; immigration-authority threats as prohibited retaliation; waiver void

sources.title: Housing Discrimination Under the Fair Housing Act
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development
sources.verifies: The seven federal protected classes; scope covering nearly all housing including private housing; current FHEO enforcement prioritisation guidance and withdrawn guidance documents

sources.title: Fair Housing Act Enforcement and Prioritization of Resources
sources.verifies: HUD's stated prioritisation of cases with strong evidence of intentional discrimination

sources.title: Housing Discrimination (FEHA)
sources.verifies: FEHA applies to landlords and all aspects of housing; full list of California protected characteristics including source of income, immigration status, primary language, familial status, marital status, age, military/veteran status, genetic information; protection against discrimination based on the characteristic of a family member, friend, ROOMMATE or other associate; retaliation prohibited; Section 8 voucher refusal unlawful

sources.title: File a housing discrimination complaint
sources.verifies: Federal complaint intake route a tenant can use

sources.title: HUD Fair Market Rents (40th Percentile Rents)
sources.publisher: HUD Office of Policy Development and Research
sources.verifies: Definition and statutory basis of FMRs (42 U.S.C. § 1437f; 24 CFR 888.113); FY effective date of October 1. NO area value retrieved — see Flag F-01

sources.title: Ordinance No. 265-20 (Housing Inventory and rent increase license)
sources.verifies: Codified text amending § 37.3 and adding § 37.15; the license mechanism and its suspension on non-compliance

sources.title: Ordinance Chapter 37 as amended 11/24/2024
sources.verifies: § 37.3(a)(1) 60%-of-CPI formula and 7% ceiling; § 37.3(a)(2) Banking text; § 37.3(b) notice content

sources.title: Operating & Maintenance Petition, Form 530 Schedule B
sources.verifies: O&M increase capped at 7% of base rent per petition; 7% five-year aggregate limit for properties with six or more residential units; Civ. Code § 827 notice tiers; § 37.15 license reminder

sources.title: San Francisco Property Information Map
sources.verifies: The tool SF.gov directs owners and tenants to use to establish a building's construction date and certificate of occupancy — required to close Flag F-04

sources.title: Report of Excessive Rent Increase Under the Tenant Protection Act (Form 525)
sources.verifies: The form a tenant files if they believe AB 1482 was violated; the Rent Board acknowledges receipt and informs the landlord of the applicable law but cannot enforce state law or hold AB 1482 hearings

sources.title: Rent Board News
sources.verifies: The authoritative current-announcements feed; used to detect new law and to confirm the 1.6% rate and the 4.2% deposit rate announcements

sources.title: Update to Algorithmic Devices Law (October 6, 2025)
sources.verifies: From 2025-10-06 tenants' rights organisations may ALSO sue to enforce § 37.10C, alongside the City Attorney and individual tenants; File No. 240796

sources.title: New Legislation Expands Tenant Protections Related to Residential Demolitions and Major Renovations (January 23, 2026)
sources.verifies: Effective 2026-02-09: new just cause § 37.9(a)(17); § 37.9(a)(10) narrowed to a single unit; mandatory replacement of demolished units; five-year demolition bar after harassment or a non-compliant buyout; 45-day investigative harassment hearings; up to 39 months of additional relocation for § 37.9(a)(11) displacement over three months; OMI one-year rebuttable presumption

sources.title: The San Francisco Rent Board has moved (March 18, 2025)
sources.verifies: Confirms 25 Van Ness Avenue, Suite 700, San Francisco, CA 94102 as the CURRENT office address — resolves Flag F-17

sources.title: New Interest Rate for Security Deposits Effective 3/1/26 (January 9, 2026)
sources.verifies: Independently confirms the 4.2% security deposit interest rate for 3/1/2026 – 2/28/2027

sources.title: Rent Ordinance Section 37.3 was amended effective November 24, 2024 (Ordinance No. 248-24)
sources.verifies: Ordinance 248-24 changes the new-construction date in the Rent Ordinance, but only if Costa-Hawkins is repealed or amended to permit the City to do so — relevant context for Flag F-04

sources.title: Unlawful Detainers will require a 10 day response starting January 1, 2025 (AB 2347)
sources.verifies: AB 2347 changed the tenant response time to an unlawful detainer complaint from five days to ten days
